# uptimekuma_maintenance (Resource)

A maintenance window. While it is active, the monitors it covers are shown as under maintenance instead of down, and their notifications are suppressed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "uptimekuma_monitor_http" "web" {
  name = "Web"
  url  = "https://example.com"
}

# Recurring weekly window: Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 02:00 to 04:30.
resource "uptimekuma_maintenance" "weekly_patching" {
  title       = "Weekly patching"
  description = "OS updates and reboots"
  strategy    = "recurring-weekday"
  weekdays    = [1, 3, 5]
  start_time  = "02:00"
  end_time    = "04:30"
  timezone    = "Europe/Lisbon"

  monitor_ids = [uptimekuma_monitor_http.web.id]
}

# One-off window with a fixed start and end.
resource "uptimekuma_maintenance" "migration" {
  title       = "Database migration"
  description = "Moving to the new cluster"
  strategy    = "single"
  start_date  = "2026-09-12 22:00"
  end_date    = "2026-09-13 02:00"

  monitor_ids = [uptimekuma_monitor_http.web.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `description` (String) Description of the maintenance.
- `strategy` (String) How the window is scheduled: `manual`, `single`, `cron`, `recurring-interval`, `recurring-weekday` or `recurring-day-of-month`.
- `title` (String) Title shown on status pages and in the dashboard.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the window is active. Set to false to pause it. Default: true.
- `cron` (String) Cron expression for the `cron` strategy. For the recurring strategies the server derives one from the schedule and reports it here.
- `days_of_month` (Set of Number) Days of the month for `recurring-day-of-month`, from 1 to 31.
- `duration_minutes` (Number) How long the window lasts, in minutes. Required for the `cron` strategy.
- `end_date` (String) End of the window, in the same format as `start_date`.
- `end_time` (String) Daily end time for recurring strategies, as `HH:MM`.
- `interval_day` (Number) Interval in days for `recurring-interval`.
- `monitor_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the monitors this window covers. Uptime Kuma replaces the whole set on each save.
- `start_date` (String) Start of the window, for the `single` strategy and as the lower bound of recurring ones. Format: `2026-01-31 22:00`.
- `start_time` (String) Daily start time for recurring strategies, as `HH:MM`.
- `status_page_ids` (Set of Number) Numeric IDs of the status pages that should show this window. Use the `page_id` attribute of `uptimekuma_status_page`. Uptime Kuma replaces the whole set on each save.
- `timezone` (String) Timezone the schedule is interpreted in, or `SAME_AS_SERVER`. Default: `SAME_AS_SERVER`.
- `weekdays` (Set of Number) Days of the week for `recurring-weekday`, where 0 is Sunday.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Numeric ID of the maintenance window, assigned by Uptime Kuma.
- `status` (String) Current state as computed by the server, for example `under-maintenance`, `scheduled` or `ended`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Monitors, tags, notifications and the rest are imported by their numeric ID,
# which is visible in the Uptime Kuma URL when you open the object.
terraform import uptimekuma_maintenance.example 2
```
